top_deficiency_types.title: Protect each resident from all types of abuse such as physical, mental, sexual abuse, physical punishment, and neglect by anybody.
top_deficiency_types.category: Freedom from Abuse, Neglect, and Exploitation Deficiencies

top_deficiency_types.title: Ensure that a nursing home area is free from accident hazards and provides adequate supervision to prevent accidents.
top_deficiency_types.category: Quality of Life and Care Deficiencies

top_deficiency_types.title: Develop and implement a complete care plan that meets all the resident's needs, with timetables and actions that can be measured.
top_deficiency_types.category: Resident Assessment and Care Planning Deficiencies

top_deficiency_types.title: Provide enough food/fluids to maintain a resident's health.
top_deficiency_types.category: Quality of Life and Care Deficiencies

top_deficiency_types.title: Ensure that nurses and nurse aides have the appropriate competencies to care for every resident in a way that maximizes each resident's well being.
Ensure residents have reasonable access to and privacy in their use of communication methods.
Provide safe and appropriate respiratory care for a resident when needed.
top_deficiency_types.category: Quality of Life and Care Deficiencies

top_deficiency_types.title: Provide and implement an infection prevention and control program.
Ensure that each resident is free from the use of physical restraints, unless needed for medical treatment.
top_deficiency_types.category: Freedom from Abuse, Neglect, and Exploitation Deficiencies

top_deficiency_types.title: Try different approaches before using a bed rail.  If a bed rail is needed, the facility must (1) assess a resident for safety risk; (2) review these risks and benefits with the resident/representative; (3) get informed consent; and (4) Correctly install and maintain the bed rail.
top_deficiency_types.category: Quality of Life and Care Deficiencies
